questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A solid metallic sphere of radius 10.5 cm is melted and recast into a number of smaller cones, each of radius 3.5 cm and height 3 cm. Find the number of cones so formed.
questions.solution: Number of cones = volume of sphere ÷ volume of one cone = [(4/3)π × 10.5³] ÷ [(1/3)π × 3.5² × 3] = (4 × 1157.625)/(36.75) = 4630.5/36.75 = 126.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Find the value of m for which the quadratic equation (m − 1) x² + 2 (m − 1) x + 1 = 0 has two real and equal roots.
questions.solution: Equal roots need D = 0: [2(m − 1)]² − 4(m − 1) = 4(m − 1)(m − 2) = 0, so m = 1 or m = 2. m = 1 makes the equation not quadratic, so m = 2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The product of Rehan's age (in years) 5 years ago and his age 7 years from now, is one more than twice his present age. Find his present age.
questions.solution: Let his present age be x. (x − 5)(x + 7) = 2x + 1, so x² + 2x − 35 = 2x + 1 and x² = 36. Age is positive, so x = 6 years.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Two concentric circles are of radii 4 cm and 3 cm. Find the length of the chord of the larger circle which touches the smaller circle.
questions.solution: The radius of the smaller circle to the point of contact is perpendicular to the chord and bisects it. Half the chord = √(4² − 3²) = √7 cm, so the chord is 2√7 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The angle of elevation of the top of a building from the foot of the tower is 30° and the angle of elevation of the top of the tower from the foot of the building is 60°. If the tower is 50 m high, then find the height of the building.
questions.solution: Let the distance between them be d. From the foot of the building, tan 60° = 50/d, so d = 50/√3. From the foot of the tower, the building's height h = d tan 30° = (50/√3)(1/√3) = 50/3 ≈ 16.67 m.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: From a point on a bridge across a river, the angles of depression of the banks on opposite sides of the river are 30° and 45° respectively. If the bridge is at a height of 3 m from the banks, then find the width of the river.
questions.solution: Horizontal distance to one bank = 3/tan 30° = 3√3 m and to the other = 3/tan 45° = 3 m. Width = 3 + 3√3 = 3(1 + √3) m ≈ 8.19 m.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: From a solid cylinder of height 30 cm and radius 7 cm, a conical cavity of height 24 cm and same radius is hollowed out. Find the total surface area of the remaining solid.
questions.solution: The cone's slant height = √(24² + 7²) = 25 cm. Remaining surface = curved surface of cylinder + bottom circle + curved surface of cone = 2π(7)(30) + π(7²) + π(7)(25) = π(420 + 49 + 175) = 644π = 644 × 22/7 = 2024 cm².

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Water in a canal, 8 m wide and 6 m deep, is flowing with a speed of 12 km/hour. How much area will it irrigate in one hour, if 0.05 m of standing water is required ?
questions.solution: Water flowing in one hour = 8 × 6 × 12000 = 576000 m³. Area irrigated = 576000 ÷ 0.05 = 11520000 m² (1152 hectares).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A triangle ABC with ∠B = 90° is given. Taking AB as diameter, a circle has been drawn intersecting AC at point P. Prove that the tangent drawn at point P bisects BC.
questions.solution: Let the tangent at P meet BC at Q. Since ∠B = 90°, BC is tangent to the circle at B, so QB = QP (tangents from Q) and ∠QBP = ∠QPB. ∠APB = 90° (angle in a semicircle), so ∠BPC = 90°. In right Δ BPC, ∠QCP = 90° − ∠QBP and ∠QPC = 90° − ∠QPB, so ∠QCP = ∠QPC and QP = QC. Hence QB = QP = QC, so Q is the mid-point of BC.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Gadisar Lake is located in the Jaisalmer district of Rajasthan. The lake has many Chhatris. From a point A h m above from water level, the angle of elevation of top of Chhatri (point B) is 45° and angle of depression of its reflection in water (point C) is 60°. If the height of Chhatri above water level is (approximately) 10 m, then find the height (h) of the point A above water level. (Use √3 = 1.73)
questions.solution: Let d be the horizontal distance from A to the Chhatri. B is 10 m above water and its reflection C is 10 m below. tan 45° = (10 − h)/d gives d = 10 − h. tan 60° = (10 + h)/d gives √3(10 − h) = 10 + h, so h = 10(√3 − 1)/(√3 + 1) = 20 − 10√3 = 20 − 17.3 = 2.7 m.
